claim: The Legislature convenes in regular session every year on the second Monday in January
quote: The legislature shall meet in regular session annually commencing on the second Monday in January

claim: Even-year sessions are limited to 90 calendar days unless extended by two-thirds of each house; odd-year sessions have no limit
quote: The duration of regular sessions held in even-numbered years shall not exceed ninety calendar days

claim: Bills are presented to the governor within ten days after passage
quote: Within ten days after passage, every bill shall be signed by the presiding officers and presented to the governor

claim: A bill not returned within ten calendar days after presentment becomes law without signature
quote: If any bill shall not be returned within ten calendar days (excluding the day presented) after it shall have been presented to the governor, it shall become a law

claim: The governor may call a special session
quote: The governor may, on extraordinary occasions, call the legislature into special session by proclamation

claim: Acts take effect on publication of the session laws unless the act says otherwise
quote: Such acts shall take effect and be in force from and after such publication, unless otherwise specifically provided in such act.

claim: The session laws publication date is July 1 when the volume is ready by then
quote: shall be July 1 if a limited number of the volume are in the office of the secretary of state on or before July 1

claim: Municipal primaries are the first Tuesday in August and general elections the Tuesday after the first Monday in November of odd-numbered years
quote: shall be held on the Tuesday succeeding the first Monday in November of 2017 of odd-numbered years and on such date thereafter

claim: "Municipality" for election timing includes cities and consolidated city-counties
quote: Any city, consolidated city-county created under

claim: "Municipality" also includes school districts, community colleges and drainage, extension, irrigation, improvement, water and hospital districts
quote: community college, drainage district, extension district created under

claim: Special districts that elect their board at a district meeting are excluded
quote: The term does not include any special district where the election of members of the governing body is conducted at a meeting of the special district.

claim: Cities and hospital districts may also hold elections in even-numbered years to stagger terms or use three-year terms
quote: Cities and hospital districts may provide for elections of elected officials in even-numbered years in order to provide for staggered terms of office or for three-year terms of office

claim: Each municipality sets its terms of office by ordinance or resolution to fit the schedule
quote: The governing body of the municipality shall establish by ordinance or resolution terms of office of elected officials to comply with this act.

claim: A municipal candidate may file a declaration of intent with the county election officer with a fee
quote: may become a candidate for municipal office by filing a declaration of intent to become a candidate with the county election officer

claim: Old city ordinances on election timing did not survive the 2015 move to November
quote: except those provisions relating to the timing of city primary and general elections

claim: City general elections are held on the Tuesday after the first Monday in November, if needed, in both odd and even years
quote: The general election of city officers shall be held on the Tuesday following the first Monday in November of each odd-numbered and even-numbered years, if needed.

claim: A city primary is held only where a district has more than three candidates
quote: if there are more than three qualified candidates for any member district

claim: An at-large city primary is held only where candidates exceed three times the seats
quote: if there are more than three times the number of candidates as there are members to be elected

claim: School board general elections are in November of odd-numbered years with an August primary
quote: Board member general elections shall be held on the Tuesday following the first Monday in November of odd-numbered years.

claim: A school board primary is held only where a member position has more than three candidates
quote: if there are more than three qualified candidates for any member position in any member district

claim: A unified school district board has seven members serving four-year terms, unless a specific law provides otherwise
quote: a board of education composed of seven (7) members

claim: County and state partisan primaries are the first Tuesday of August in even-numbered years
quote: The primary national, state, county and township election shall be held on the first Tuesday of August in even-numbered years

claim: The general election is the Tuesday after the first Monday in November
quote: means the elections held on the Tuesday succeeding the first Monday in November of both odd-numbered and even-numbered years

claim: Township elections are held in November of even-numbered years in every township except city townships
quote: a township election shall be held in each township in the state, except in city townships

claim: Township trustee and treasurer are elected together for four-year terms
quote: there shall be elected for a term of four years, a township trustee and a treasurer

claim: The township clerk is elected for four years on the alternate cycle
quote: each fourth year thereafter, there shall be elected for a term of four years, a township clerk

claim: County and township candidates are nominated by party primary or by independent petition
quote: all candidates for national, state, county and township offices shall be nominated by

claim: Parties whose governor candidate polled under 5% nominate by convention instead of primary
quote: did not poll at least 5% of the total vote cast for all candidates for governor in the preceding general election

claim: A candidate cannot run in a party primary and then as an independent for county or township office in the same cycle
quote: shall file for office as a partisan candidate in a primary election and also file for office as an independent candidate

claim: Affiliated voters vote in their party primary; each party decides by January 15 whether unaffiliated voters may vote in its primary
quote: whether voters who are unaffiliated with such political party may vote in such party's primary election

claim: An unaffiliated voter can declare a party at the polls and receive that party ballot, which records the affiliation
quote: Such a statement of party affiliation shall constitute a declaration of party affiliation

claim: Party affiliation cannot be changed between the candidate filing deadline and certification of primary results
quote: Such declaration cannot be filed during the time from the candidate filing deadline

claim: City elections are partisan or nonpartisan as the city governing body decides
quote: City elections shall be nonpartisan or partisan as determined by the governing body

claim: School board elections are always nonpartisan
quote: School elections shall be nonpartisan and laws applicable only to partisan elections shall not apply in such elections.

claim: The candidate with the most votes wins unless a law expressly says otherwise
quote: the person having the highest number of votes for any office shall be deemed to have been elected to that office

claim: The independent-nomination statute does not apply to city and school elections
quote: This section shall not apply to city and school elections, nor to election of other officers provided by law to be elected in odd-numbered years.

claim: A voter who holds a party affiliation cannot accept an independent nomination
quote: shall be eligible to accept an independent nomination for any office

claim: Township offices also have an independent petition route
quote: Independent nominations of candidates for offices to be filled by the voters of a township

claim: Independent petition signers must live in the same county and election district as the office
quote: All signers of each separate nomination petition shall reside in the same county and election district of the office sought.

claim: A voter may not sign independent petitions for more than one candidate for the same office
quote: No person shall join in nominating more than one person for the same office

claim: Each city sets by ordinance how many signatures a city nomination petition needs
quote: shall be established by the city governing body by passage of an ordinance

claim: City elections are run by the county election officer of the county holding most of the city population
quote: or of the county in which the greater population of the city is located if the city extends into more than one county

claim: A board of county commissioners has three, five or seven members
quote: The board of county commissioners of each county shall consist of three, five or seven qualified electors.

claim: Each commissioner lives in and represents a district
quote: one county commissioner shall reside in and represent each commissioner district within the county

claim: Commissioners serve staggered four-year terms
quote: all county commissioners shall hold office for a term of four years

claim: Changing the number of commissioner districts needs voter approval
quote: shall take effect until it has been approved by a majority of the qualified electors of the county voting thereon

claim: Sherman County may elect its commissioners at large
quote: Each county commissioner shall run at large.

claim: Each county elects a county clerk for four years
quote: a county clerk shall be elected in each county, for a term of four (4) years

claim: Each county elects a county treasurer for four years
quote: a county treasurer shall be elected in each county for a term of four (4) years

claim: Each county elects a register of deeds for four years
quote: a register of deeds shall be elected in each county for a term of four (4) years

claim: Each county elects a county attorney for four years, except as otherwise provided by law
quote: a county attorney shall be elected in each county who shall hold office for a term of four (4) years

claim: Each county elects a sheriff for four years except counties under a consolidated law enforcement act
quote: Except in those counties operating under the provisions of any consolidated law enforcement act

claim: The constitution requires an elected sheriff except in a county that abolished the office before January 11, 2022
quote: shall not apply to a county that abolished the office of sheriff prior to January 11, 2022

claim: County home rule is exercised by commission resolution, and counties remain subject to all state election law
quote: Counties shall be subject to all acts of the legislature concerning elections, election commissioners and officers and their duties as such officers and the election of county officers.

claim: Only counties designated urban areas may adopt a charter; Johnson and Sedgwick are so designated
quote: The area comprising Sedgwick county is hereby designated as an urban area

claim: Johnson County is designated an urban area
quote: The area comprising Johnson county is hereby designated as an urban area

claim: A county charter may set the number, terms and method of election of commissioners
quote: fix the number, term, and compensation of the commissioners and their method of election

claim: A county charter may make elected county offices appointive or eliminate them
quote: authorize the appointment of or elimination of elective officials and offices within the charter

claim: State law provided for consolidating Kansas City, Kansas, and Wyandotte County
quote: Consolidation of Kansas City, Kansas, and Wyandotte county

claim: The Unified Government of Wyandotte County/Kansas City exists and is headed by a chief executive/mayor
quote: Chief executive/mayor of unified government of Wyandotte County

claim: The consolidation plan decides whether the governing body is elected on a partisan or nonpartisan basis
quote: determine whether elections of the governing body of the consolidated city-county shall be partisan or nonpartisan elections

claim: Bonner Springs, Edwardsville and Lake Quivira stay separate cities inside Wyandotte County
quote: except the territory of the cities of Bonner Springs, Edwardsville, Lake Quivira and the unincorporated area of the county

claim: State law also allows unification of governments in Greeley County
quote: Unification of governmental units in Greeley county

claim: A Greeley County unification plan decides partisan or nonpartisan elections
quote: determine whether elections of the governing body of the unified city-county shall be partisan or nonpartisan elections

claim: The legislature may set up to four classes of cities
quote: the legislature may establish not to exceed four classes of cities

claim: Cities have constitutional home rule over local affairs and government
quote: Cities are hereby empowered to determine their local affairs and government

claim: A charter ordinance cannot exempt a city from laws that apply uniformly to all cities
quote: other than enactments of statewide concern applicable uniformly to all cities, other enactments applicable uniformly to all cities

claim: A city over 15,000 becomes first class by governor proclamation after certifying its population
quote: who shall thereupon by public proclamation declare such city to be a city of the first class

claim: A city between 15,000 and 25,000 may choose to stay second class
quote: would be more advantageous for such city to continue to operate as a city of the second class

claim: Second class covers cities over 2,000 and under 15,000
quote: all cities hereafter attaining a population of more than 2,000 and less than 15,000

claim: A city between 2,000 and 5,000 may choose to stay third class
quote: would be more advantageous for such city to continue to operate as a city of the third class

claim: When a city becomes second class, its land leaves the township
quote: land within the corporate limits of such city is no longer located within the territory of any township

claim: Third class covers places of not more than 2,000, plus county seats of any size that were unincorporated towns
quote: containing not more than two thousand inhabitants

claim: A second-class city reduced to 1,000 or fewer people returns to third class only by a vote of its residents
quote: has been reduced in population to one thousand or less

claim: A third-class city elects a mayor and five council members for two-year terms by default
quote: Every two years an election shall be held for a mayor, and five council members.

claim: A second-class city elects a mayor, council members and a city treasurer for two-year terms by default
quote: a mayor, council members and city treasurer

claim: The second-class city statute still names an April election date that the 2015 municipal timing law superseded
quote: there shall be elected on the first Tuesday in April of each odd-numbered year

claim: A city adopts or abandons a form of government by a vote of its residents
quote: the question of the adoption or abandonment of the form of city government shall be submitted to the qualified electors of the city

claim: The modified mayor-council form has a mayor, three council members at large and four by district
quote: The governing body shall consist of a mayor and three (3) members of the council elected at large and four (4) members of the council
